description: P3 consumer-assertion over CHECK 15's own machinery in tools/policy_check.sh. CHECK 15 is the structural guard that keeps Claude Code permission-engine claims single-homed: the claim token may appear only under an allowlisted surface, with the Findings section of docs/adr/0010-permission-allowlist-posture.md as the single authoritative home. Three pins, each covering a distinct way the guard dies. (1) source pins the '=== CHECK 15:' section header line together with its title, so deleting or renaming the check turns the suite red. (2) The consumer pins the per-occurrence finding emitter — add_finding 'CHECK15' with its scanned-file and line-number arguments — so gutting the check's ability to REPORT while leaving its header intact is caught; this is the emitter that reports a real violation, distinct from the fail-closed zero-occurrence emitter, which passes the authority doc instead and is deliberately not what this pin matches. (3) set_check pins THE ALLOWLIST ITSELF, and mode is `equal` rather than `superset` BY DESIGN: the threat model here is someone SILENTLY WIDENING the allowlist so an inconvenient finding goes away. A presence pin and a `superset` set_check can both only notice a REMOVED surface; only `equal` fails on an ADDED one (README rule 6). That single choice is what makes this fixture guard the guard rather than merely witness it. The extract_regex is anchored on the `# CHECK15-ALLOW` structural marker and captures the quoted entry via a NEGATED-DELIMITER class ([^'\n]) rather than a positive charset, so an oddly-spelled or unexpected entry surfaces as an extra instead of being silently skipped; the quotes are captured with the entry so that an empty-string entry — which would allowlist every path in the repository — cannot capture as the empty string the extras scan drops. This fixture does NOT catch: (a) CHECK 15 NEUTERED INTERNALLY while its header, its emitter and its allowlist literals all stay intact — narrowing the find(1) scan set, retargeting CHECK15_TOKEN, or wrapping the emitter in a condition that never fires all leave every pin green, and that is a real residual, not a theoretical one; (b) a widening authored WITHOUT the `# CHECK15-ALLOW` marker comment, or outside the CHECK15_ALLOWLIST array entirely, since extract_regex is line-scoped and anchored on that marker; (c) a duplicate of an expected entry, because set membership dedupes; (d) the paraphrase residual CHECK 15 itself accepts — a surface that restates engine behavior without ever spelling the trigger token; (e) drift in files this fixture does not name — `files` is a LITERAL list with NO glob expansion, so it blocks removal and drift in tools/policy_check.sh and is blind to any check machinery relocated elsewhere. Both halves of (e) are true, and the protection is worth having despite the blind half. Residual by construction: the consumer pin embeds the emitter's variable names, so renaming CHECK 15's internal scan variables trips it and requires a conscious re-pin.
